questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: How a suspension prepares and resolves
questions.learningObjective: Identify the consonant preparation of a suspension
questions.stem: A chef costing sheet lists a suspension prepared on a consonant note; which step best describes its resolution?

options.text: The suspended note resolves downward by step to a consonance
The suspended note leaps upward to the next chord tone
options.misconception: treats resolution as an upward leap

options.text: The suspended note stays put and the bass moves
The suspended note resolves by skipping a third
options.misconception: confuses stepwise resolution with a skip

questions.explanation: A suspension prepares a note as a consonance, sounds it as a dissonance against the new bass, then resolves downward by step. Leaping or skipping misrepresents the required stepwise motion.

answer.exemplar: A stated key contains seven diatonic chords; two chords that do not fit are borrowed or chromatic chords such as a Neapolitan sixth or an augmented sixth, which introduce pitches outside the key signature and create colour or tension.

questions.explanation: Foreign chords introduce non-diatonic pitches and functions, so they do not belong to the stated key. Diatonic chords alone fit the key.

questions.topic: The distance a ninth falls as it resolves
questions.stem: A recipe sheet counts semitones a minor ninth falls resolving to the octave; how many?
questions.explanation: A minor ninth resolves down by a minor second of one semitone to the octave. The step size is one semitone.
